exchanges.reply:
I checked the OKF v0.2 spec and our docs. First, a correction: I said earlier that `docs/phase-5-checklist.md` and `docs/unicorn-perks-plan.md` don't exist. They do. My file listing was cut off, so the `CONTEXT-MAP.md` links are fine.

## What OKF is
OKF is a set of rules for ordinary Markdown in git, not a tool or service. There's nothing to host or connect.
- **Required:** every `.md` file needs YAML frontmatter with a `type` field, e.g. `type: Plan`.
- **Optional:** fields like `title`, `description`, `tags`, `status` (`draft | stable | deprecated`), `verified`, `stale_after` and `sources`.
- **Two reserved files:**
  - `index.md`: a bullet list of a folder's contents. Only the top-level one may declare `okf_version: "0.2"`.
  - `log.md`: dated change history, newest first.
- **Links:** ordinary Markdown links, preferably starting with `/` (measured from the docs root).
- **Leniency:** tools that read OKF must accept unknown types and broken links.

## What it would take

| # | Step | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Decide which folder holds the docs.** I'd use `docs/`. Using the repo root would pull in every skill file and the 1,095-line `README.md`. | decision |
| 2 | **Add frontmatter** to about 17 docs: `docs/*`, `docs/legacy/*`, `docs/agents/*`, both `CONTEXT.md` glossaries, the two token-search docs, and `CONTEXT-MAP.md`. Pick a small set of types: `Glossary`, `Architecture Review`, `Spec`, `Roadmap`, `Plan`, `Checklist`, `Design Notes`, `Agent Config`, `ADR`. | small |
| 3 | **Turn existing status notes into fields.** The "Archived (2026-06-30)" notes on the legacy checklists become `status: deprecated`, the "partially superseded" note on `core-spec.md` becomes `status` plus `stale_after`, and the "checked against the code on 2026-06-30" note becomes `verified`. | small |
| 4 | **Add `index.md` files** in `docs/`, `docs/legacy/` and `docs/agents/`. `CONTEXT-MAP.md`'s list of planning docs becomes the top-level `docs/index.md`. `docs/legacy/README.md` becomes `docs/legacy/index.md` plus a `log.md`. | small |
| 5 | **Decide where the glossaries live.** They currently sit in `src/` and `src-tauri/`, outside `docs/`. Either move them into the docs folder (e.g. `docs/contexts/`) and update `docs/agents/domain.md`, or leave them in place and link out to them. | decision |
| 6 | **Teach the skills that create docs.** `domain-modeling` writes `CONTEXT.md` and ADR files from its templates (`CONTEXT-FORMAT.md`, `ADR-FORMAT.md`), which don't include OKF frontmatter. Those templates exist in both `.claude/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, and editing them means they drift from Matt's originals. | small, ongoing |
| 7 | **Add a checker:** a small script, run before each commit or in CI, that confirms every doc has a `type`. Without one, the format will quietly stop being followed. | small |

All told it's roughly half a day, nearly all of it frontmatter and index files. Nothing in the app code changes.

## What it means for us
- **Upside:** our docs already look a lot like this: one file per concept, dated status notes, a map of contexts. OKF makes the status machine-readable, so any agent (Claude, Cursor, or another tool) can tell what's current and what's stale without reading the prose notes. It stays in git, adds no infrastructure, and doesn't tie us to a vendor.
- **Cost:** every new doc needs frontmatter, and index files have to be kept current. That's the reason for the checker and the template edits.
- **Overlap with Linear:** OKF is for knowledge and Linear is now for work. `phase-5-checklist.md` and `TOKEN_SEARCH_CHECKLIST.md` are really task lists. I'd move their open items into Linear issues and keep only the plans and specs as docs.
- **Maturity:** the spec is at v0.2 and recently had breaking changes (v0.1's `timestamp` field became `generated`), so expect some further churn.

Two things to fix along the way: `AGENTS.md` probably still points at GitHub Issues, since we only updated `CLAUDE.md`, and the Linear changes from earlier are still uncommitted.

Should I go ahead with `docs/` as the docs folder and the glossaries moved into it, or would you rather settle steps 1 and 5 differently first?

- [OKF Spec — okf.md](https://okf.md/spec/)

exchanges.prompt: I'm on free plan, will affect it?
tools: WebSearch Linear free plan 250 issue limit archived issues count
exchanges.reply:
Yes, a bit, but both options still work. The Free plan allows **2 teams** and **250 active issues** (archived issues don't count).

- **Option A (new team):** this uses your **second and last** team slot, since you already have Ssventitsky. A third repo would then need either Option B or a paid plan. The issue limit is shared across the whole workspace, so a new team doesn't give you more issues.
- **Option B (rename `SSV`):** costs nothing, but every issue on the team gets the new prefix.

**Issue limit:** you have about 18 issues, so 250 is a long way off. Once you hit it you can't create new issues, which would break the issue-filing skills (`to-issues`, `qa`, `triage`). Linear auto-archives closed issues after a while, so this mainly matters if the backlog keeps growing.

**My recommendation:** if this repo is your main project in Linear, use Option A with a short key like `AF`. If you expect to track several repos, rename `SSV` instead (or keep it) and tell repos apart by project, saving the second team slot. What do you want to do?

Sources:

- [Linear Docs — Billing and plans](https://linear.app/docs/billing-and-plans)

## 1. `README.md`: rewrite (1,095 lines down to about 100)
- **It's mostly duplicates.** Lines 1–74 and 75–148 are identical copies of the overview. Lines 149–404 are a third, different version. Lines 405–1095 are an older, longer form of what's now in `docs/core-spec.md`, `extended-roadmap.md` and `design-notes.md`.
- **Much of it is wrong:**
  - It says "not scaffolded yet", but phases 1–4 are done.
  - It gives `npm` commands; the project uses `pnpm`.
  - It lists React 18 and plain rusqlite; the code uses React 19 and Diesel.
  - It says the default hotkey is `Ctrl+Shift+D`; it's `F9`.
  - It claims the API key is bundled with the app; the key comes only from environment variables.
  - It lists the wrong dependencies and a folder layout that doesn't exist.
  - It leaves out two environment variables, `OVERLAY_HOTKEY` and `REQUIRE_DESTINY_FOCUS`.
- **Some detail exists nowhere else and needs saving first:** interface sketches for future features, data sources (d2foundry, Clarity), the format of DIM wishlists, search by stat thresholds and source, and the note that BattlEye bans for memory access. I'd move these into the matching docs before cutting the README.

**What the rule says:** `.cursor/rules/react-radix-shadcn.mdc` tells agents to use Radix and shadcn/ui before writing their own UI parts such as dialogs, dropdowns, tooltips and popovers. If the project doesn't have them yet, it says to install them.

**What the code actually does:**
- `@radix-ui/react-dialog` is a dependency, but nothing imports it. I left it in place during SSV-23 for this reason.
- shadcn isn't set up: there is no `components.json` and no `src/components/ui/`.
- The UI is hand-built. For example, `src/components/Tooltip.tsx` is a custom tooltip, and the search dropdown has its own keyboard handling.

If I share the rule as written, Claude Code will start adding Radix and shadcn on its next UI task, which pulls against the existing code.

**Your options:**
1. **Adopt Radix/shadcn:** keep the rule and treat the custom parts as things to migrate over time. Most accessible, but it means a new dependency stack and its default styles to fit around your `af-*` tokens.
2. **Stay custom:** drop the rule, remove the unused `@radix-ui/react-dialog`, and write down "build our own, using `af-*` tokens" as the convention.
3. **Middle ground:** use bare Radix primitives (no shadcn) only for the hard accessibility cases like dialogs, focus traps and popovers, and keep everything else custom.

For a small overlay with its own visual style, I'd recommend option 3: you get correct focus and keyboard behavior where it's hard to get right, without adopting shadcn's styling. Once you pick, I'll finish SSV-21 and link the conventions from `AGENTS.md`.

exchanges.prompt: do those fully customizable components?
exchanges.reply:
Yes, both are fully customizable, in different ways.

**Radix primitives: you control all the styling, they control the behavior.**
- They ship with no styles. Every part (`Dialog.Content`, `Popover.Trigger` and so on) is a plain element you style with your own classes, including `af-*` tokens.
- What they handle for you is the hard part: focus trapping, focus return, Esc and outside-click dismissal, ARIA attributes, keyboard navigation, and rendering in a portal.
- You can override that behavior through props, not by editing it:
  - `onEscapeKeyDown` / `onPointerDownOutside` with `preventDefault()` to block dismissal.
  - `modal={false}` to turn off the focus trap.
  - `forceMount` to keep content mounted for animations.
  - `asChild` to render through your own element instead of theirs.
- So it's very flexible, but you're working inside their behavior model.

**shadcn/ui: not a library. It copies source files into your repo.**
- The CLI writes the component code (Radix plus Tailwind classes) into `src/components/ui/`, and from then on you own it. You can edit anything: markup, classes, behavior.
- The catch is the starting point. Its styles use shadcn's own CSS variables (`--primary`, `--muted` and so on), which you'd map to or replace with your `af-*` tokens.
- Recent shadcn releases also target Tailwind 4, and this repo is on Tailwind 3, so you'd have to use the older v3-compatible components or adapt them.

**What this means for this repo:**
- Radix alone fits your existing design system with no translation, since there's no foreign styling to remove.
- shadcn mostly saves typing, but much of what it would give you would be rewritten into your style anyway.
- One thing to watch: the overlay already has its own Esc handling (`desktop/esc_hook.rs` plus the search keyboard logic), and a Radix Dialog handles Esc itself. You'd connect the two with `onEscapeKeyDown`. That works, but it's a deliberate step each time.

That's why I suggested option 3: bare Radix primitives for the hard accessibility cases, custom components for everything else, and no shadcn.
